narr: An easterly wave that had been in place over southern New Mexico and Arizona all week finally tracked over New Mexico on August 20, 2022. As it did so, it brought an above normal amount of precipitation as precipitable water amounts rose to near record values. This brought widespread, beneficial rainfall to most of northern and central New Mexico with the highest 24-hour rainfall totals of two to four inches across areas south of Interstate 40 where the easterly wave tracked. The system did lack a sufficient amount of instability, and thus, stratiform rain was most common with embedded thunderstorms. These light rainfall rates meant that the traditional summertime flash flooding was not the main threat. Rather, rises on rivers, creeks, and streams were with the long duration event. Flooding was reported in Mesa along U.S. Highway 285 which stranded motorists. The McBride burn scar also experienced flooding thanks to hours of steady rainfall. Across Chaves County, the Pecos River experienced record flooding with major impacts felt for several days near Roswell, Hagerman, Dexter, and Lake Arthur.
ev: The Lincoln County emergency manager reported that hours of light, steady rainfall with totals of 1 to 2.5 inches caused burn scar flash flooding on the McBride burn scar near Ruidoso. All of Gavilan Canyon was flooded. Damages are estimated.
